summary: Created a locked-password 'opsbot' account on both node1 and node2 (RHEL 7.9), generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and confirmed opsbot@node1 can SSH into opsbot@node2 non-interactively. Discovered and fixed an sshd_config quirk on both nodes where an earlier 'PasswordAuthentication yes' directive (line 65) silently shadowed a later 'no' (OpenSSH honors the first occurrence of a keyword), so password auth was still effectively enabled; corrected the first occurrence to 'no' on both nodes, validated with 'sshd -t' and 'sshd -T', and reloaded sshd. Verified password authentication is rejected for opsbot on both nodes (server only offers publickey/gssapi) while key-based access continues to work. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured baseline boot_id/uptime and service health, rebooted node1 then node2 sequentially, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd health, opsbot account/lock state, key files, and the opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH flow after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected OS, sudo access, and sshd status on node1 and node2
Created 'opsbot' user with locked password on node1 and node2
Diagnosed sshd_config first-match-wins issue: line 65 'PasswordAuthentication yes' overrode later 'no'
Backed up sshd_config and fixed line 65 to 'no' on both nodes, validated with sshd -t and sshd -T
Generated ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1
Installed opsbot's public key into node2's opsbot authorized_keys with correct permissions/ownership
Populated opsbot's known_hosts on node1 for node2 and verified passwordless key-based SSH node1->node2
Verified password authentication is refused for opsbot on both node1 and node2 (publickey/gssapi only offered)
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service baseline on both nodes
Rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified sshd/opsbot/SSH flow recovered
Rebooted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified sshd/opsbot/authorized_keys recovered
Final end-to-end re-verification of opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 key-based SSH after both restarts

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: useradd succeeded and 'id opsbot' shows uid 1001 on both nodes

evidence.summary: Keypair generated on node1, public key installed in node2 authorized_keys, and non-interactive SSH as opsbot from node1 to node2 succeeded (whoami/hostname returned)

evidence.requirement: key-based authentication required (password auth disabled) for opsbot on both systems
evidence.summary: Found sshd_config first-directive-wins bug making 'PasswordAuthentication no' ineffective; fixed the first occurrence, validated config, reloaded sshd, and directly proved password auth is rejected for opsbot in both directions (node1->node2 and node2->node1) with server offering only publickey/gssapi; opsbot password is locked ('!!') on both nodes
Captured boot_id d72bd4ec..., sshd active, opsbot account present

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect, node became unreachable, then returned with new boot_id 715bb115... (changed from baseline), and sshd/opsbot/key-based SSH to node2 confirmed working post-restart
Captured boot_id 809708f3..., sshd active, opsbot account present

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node unreachable, then returned with new boot_id 6b9da774... (changed from baseline); sshd active with password auth disabled, opsbot account and authorized_keys intact, and final end-to-end key-based SSH from node1 to node2 succeeded
